purpose: Establish that the isolation suite can fail. Under BOPEN-GOV-EBIV-001 §4 a proposition must state the mechanism whose removal makes its evidence fail; a test that passes whether or not the mechanism is present verifies nothing. Each probe below removes one mechanism, runs the suite, and restores it.

probes.assessment: Detection holds but the message does not name the defect. With row-level security enabled and no policy present, the seeding INSERT in setUp is itself refused, so every test errors during setup rather than one assertion reporting 'tenant A read a row belonging to tenant B'. Recorded as a known gap rather than presented as a clean result. A verifier may reasonably classify this as insufficient legibility under R5; that disagreement is invited in the handoff.

probes.mechanism_removed: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on active_contexts
probes.mutation_sql: ALTER TABLE active_contexts NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
probes.observed_message: AssertionError: False is not true : active_contexts does not FORCE row level security
probes.assessment: Clean single-assertion failure naming the exact table and the exact missing property.

probes.mechanism_removed: absence of a DELETE policy on audit_events (append-only guard)
probes.mutation_sql: CREATE POLICY audit_delete_hole ON audit_events FOR DELETE USING (true);
probes.observed_message: AssertionError: 3 != 0 : an audit record was deleted
probes.assessment: Clean single-assertion failure. Incidentally informative: the permissive USING (true) clause deleted three rows rather than the one belonging to the session tenant, demonstrating that a carelessly written DELETE policy on this table would permit cross-tenant destruction of audit records, not merely local mutation.

coarse_probes.assessment: Cascading errors. Removing the policy entirely also blocks the INSERT that establishes a context, so the suite cannot reach the assertion it was meant to test. Same limitation as MUT-A. Superseded by MUT-G, which is the probe that actually isolates the read path.
Cascading errors for the same reason. Superseded by MUT-H.
Single test affected, but as an error during resource creation rather than the cross-tenant read assertion. Superseded by MUT-I.

surgical_probes.mutation_sql: ALTER POLICY active_contexts_isolation ON active_contexts USING (true);
surgical_probes.why_this_probe_is_better: Simulates a policy that is present but written wrongly, rather than one that is absent. Writes keep working, so the suite reaches the assertion it exists to make. A 'does a policy exist' check would pass against this mutation; the test does not.
surgical_probes.observed_message: AssertionError: 200 != 403 — tenant A's context was accepted under tenant B's X-Tenant-ID and a full ALLOW decision was returned

surgical_probes.mutation_sql: ALTER POLICY audit_events_read_isolation ON audit_events USING (true);
surgical_probes.observed_message: AssertionError: tenant A read an audit event belonging to tenant B
surgical_probes.note: GET /v1/audit-events contains no tenant filter in its query. This probe is what establishes that the policy — and not the handler — is what scopes the result.

surgical_probes.mutation_sql: ALTER POLICY tenant_isolation_resources ON tenant_resources USING (true);
surgical_probes.observed_message: AssertionError: 200 != 404 : tenant B read a resource owned by tenant A

supplementary_probes.question: Is the application role genuinely unable to bypass row-level security?
supplementary_probes.method: SELECT rolsuper, rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles; SELECT tablename, tableowner FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public'
supplementary_probes.result: bopen_app: rolsuper=false, rolbypassrls=false, owns none of the 11 tables (all owned by postgres)
supplementary_probes.why_it_matters: A superuser, a role with BYPASSRLS, or the table owner without FORCE would make every passing isolation result meaningless. This probe is what licenses reading the green suite as evidence.

supplementary_probes.question: Can a tenant context survive its transaction and leak to the next user of a pooled connection?
supplementary_probes.method: Open one connection, run a tenant_session for tenant A, then query the same connection outside any tenant_session
supplementary_probes.result: current_setting returned NULL and the row count was 0 — no leak
supplementary_probes.why_it_matters: platform_kernel.db claims that set_config(..., is_local => true) confines the tenant to one transaction so a pooled connection cannot carry tenant A's context into tenant B's work. That claim is a code comment until executed; this probe executes it.

provenance.executed_by: Claude (agent, Motor role) — Maker of WP-P35-01
provenance.authority: Maker record. Carries no verdict weight under BOPEN-GOV-EBIV-001 §3. Recorded so a verifier can re-run these probes rather than reconstruct them.

code_layer_probes.why_a_second_kind_of_probe_is_needed: MUT-A through MUT-I weaken database policies. A policy probe cannot reach a defence written in Python, and a code probe cannot reach one written in SQL. Both kinds are required for the suite to be adversarial across the whole stack.

probes.control_removed: unknown-kid rejection (falls back to the signing key)
probes.finding: The original test signed with a foreign key AND named a foreign kid, so it passed on the signature check alone even with the kid control removed. It was not testing what its name claimed, and the kid control had no isolating test. A test that passes for the wrong reason is indistinguishable from one that passes for the right reason until something removes the control and nothing goes red. Same failure shape as Phase 3 reporting 169/169 while RateLimitDecision violated its schema - reproduced in work written specifically to prevent it.

probes.control_removed: tenant-conflict check between token tid and X-Tenant-ID
stored-context re-read on the bearer path
probes.note: Establishes that revocation is immediate rather than delayed until token expiry.
